title: tilt-reset-shift-scratch
body:
Quick context: 06/20 morning tilt/reset shift. Short log + followups to carry forward. Mostly noisy consumer lag affecting hosted-api-embed service. Took initial actions, left TODOs for runbook edits and post-incident steps.

Timeline:
- 06:02 UTC: Pager triggered - alerts: hosted-api-embed p95 latency > 1.2s (alert rule embed-latency-p95). Initial ack by me.
- 06:04 UTC: Slack thread started in #infra-pager. Elevated to Sev2 since customer impact (queue backlog).
- 06:07 UTC: Ran curl health endpoints on embed workers: 200 but backlog metric high.
- 06:10 UTC: kubectl get pods -n hosted | grep embed -> 3/3 ready on worker pool but CPU spiking 85%.
- 06:15 UTC: Scaled embed-worker deployment +3 replicas (kubectl scale --replicas=6 deployment/embed-worker). Observed backlog begin to drop slowly.
- 06:28 UTC: p95 back to ~0.9s, alert recovered.

Actions taken (commands and checks):
- kubectl top nodes/pods to confirm CPU pressure.
- curl to /internal/metrics to inspect queue_length and kv_cache_hit. Noted kv_cache_hit dropped to 0.67 vs normal ~0.92.
- Restarted one worker (embed-worker-5) to clear suspected corrupted cache; allowed rolling restart to re-populate KV cache.
- Verified routing policy: requests were not falling back to cheaper model variants; routing config still pinned -> consider enabling transient fallback for queue bursts.

Immediate follow-ups (short):
- [ ] Draft mini-postmortem outline in INC-3421 (owner: Ravi). Capture timeline, mitigations, customer impact estimate.
- [ ] Add runbook step: if kv_cache_hit < 0.75 for >5m AND backlog>1000, trigger scale + restart pattern. (file: runbooks/embedding-service.md)
- [ ] Add explicit guidance for when to enable model fallback (who: Lena).
- [ ] Add example kubectl commands and safe rate for scaling in runbook (include rollout check).

Runbook TODOs (edit suggestions):
1) Under "triage": include quick-check list: curl /internal/metrics -> fields to inspect (queue_length, kv_cache_hit, avg_latency, inflight_requests).
2) Under "mitigation": recommend scale threshold and safe restart cadence: scale +2 replicas, wait 5m, if backlog persists then restart oldest pod.
3) Under "post-recovery": include steps to capture KV cache warmup time (run a short synthetic load job and measure p50/p95).

Questions / open items:
- Why did kv_cache_hit drop so significantly? Possible root causes: cache eviction due to memory pressure or a library regression in cache population path. Need to correlate with deploys: check GH PRs merged in past 24h (PRs: ops/pull/412 flagged).
- Is routing pinning intentional for this customer cohort? If not, make a traceable decision.

Notes to self: keep incident timeline concise, attach metrics graphs from Grafana dashboard "embed-service/shift-tilt" when drafting. Ping Samir for JVM heap checks (he has background on cache population). Schedule 30m follow-up tomorrow 09:00 local to finalize runbook edits.

Later reminders (carry-forward list):
- [ ] Run synthetic warmup after next deploy and record kv_cache_hit baseline.
- [ ] Add alert facet for kv_cache_hit dropping under X for >Y minutes.
- [ ] Create a canary config that uses model-fallback policy for 5% traffic to test graceful degradation.

End of shift blips: felt routine but kv cache anomaly needs engineering followup. Keep notes short for whoever picks this up.

Signature: Ravi K. (tilt/reset shift)
